newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban claim taking two eastern towns.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban claim taking two eastern towns.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia said it had recaptured two towns from opposition forces on Sunday in the eastern province of Kunar bordering Pakistan.

A Taleban spokesman, quoted by a Pakistan-based Afghan news service, said the militia took Shegal town, about 12 km (seven miles) east of the provincial capital Asadabad, on Sunday morning and Asmar, 30 km (18 miles) in the northeast, at midday.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted the spokesman, based in the eastern Afghan city of Jalalabad, as saying that an opposition helicopter was seen picking up bodies of an unknown number of opposition fighters killed in Asmar while one or two opposition jets bombed the area.
Two Taleban fighters were killed and two wounded while five opposition fighters were arrested in Asmar, he said.
Earlier, the Taleban spokesman said five opposition fighters had been killed and 10 captured and three Taleban fighters had been wounded during the battle for Shegal.
Asmar had been in the hands of anti-Taleban forces since early April and Shegal since mid-April.

AIP said clashes in the area during the past three weeks had cost at least 15 Taleban dead, including a commander known as Arabistan, and more than 30 wounded. It put opposition losses in the same period at 21 killed and more than 50 wounded.
The Taleban have been trying to quell an uprising in Kunar province involving Kashmir Khan, a commander of the Hizb-i-Islami guerrilla faction, and disaffected tribesmen.

The militia, which seized the capital Kabul in September and controls about three-quarters of Afghanistan, is also fighting former government forces led by Ahmad Shah Masood and the Uzbek troops of General Abdul Rashid Dostum in northern provinces.
